title: Freya and the Thorn
premise: Xanthe Fairweather, exiled storm-caller and charm-seller, discovers that the crown's new magic hunt is a cover for a darker bargain: the court beneath the mountain has been feeding stolen souls to the sleeping Thorn, an ancient root of power that grants the throne its dominion. When Xanthe learns her own sister's soul was sold to the court twenty years ago—the price of Xanthe's exile—she joins a smuggler's crew to steal it back before the moon completes its thirteenth turn and the Thorn wakes fully. Betrayed by the smuggler she trusted, Xanthe must choose between reclaiming her own stolen memories of the night her sister was sold and destroying the Thorn at the cost of every soul it holds, including her sister's. In the end she splits the difference: she shatters the Thorn with a final storm, releasing the souls into the moon's light, but the effort strips her of her magic—and her sister's soul passes through her one last time, whispering forgiveness, before the court beneath the mountain collapses into ruin.
about_author: Coral Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in coastal fishing towns before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about memory, inheritance, and the quiet violence of institutions, and she still cannot resist a good storm.

chapters.title: Salt and Small Wonders
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the port city of Greyharbor, Xanthe sells luck-knots and weather charms to fishermen, hiding her storm-calling behind a merchant's smile. A raid on the market street forces her to smother a storm rising in her chest. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of hiding, and the first crack in her careful life.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Proclamation
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Criers announce the crown's hunt for the gifted: registration, then seizure. Xanthe prepares to flee Greyharbor but lingers for one last customer—a girl whose charm Xanthe recognizes as her own sister's handiwork. Emotional beat: dread sharpened into purpose; the past knocking.

chapters.title: What the Charm Knew
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The girl, Wren, reveals her charm came from a dying woman in the mountain town of Hollowmere, who spoke of souls sold to the court beneath the mountain. Xanthe recognizes the knot-work: it is her sister Isolde's. Emotional beat: grief reopened, a thread pulled.

chapters.title: The Saltwife's Offer
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe seeks out Maren the Saltwife, an old smuggler who once moved the gifted across the border. Maren offers passage to Hollowmere with her crew—but warns that the mountain road is watched and that the court buys loyalty cheaply. Emotional beat: wary hope, the price of trust.

chapters.title: Crew of the Drowned Lantern
chapters.summary: Multiple POV, mostly Xanthe. Aboard the smuggler barque, Xanthe meets the crew: the taciturn helmsman Corvin, the sharp-tongued navigator Pell, and the charming first mate Ash, who watches her too closely. A storm forces Xanthe to use her gift to save the ship, exposing her. Emotional beat: belonging glimpsed, then threatened by revelation.

chapters.title: Storm Oath
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Instead of turning her in, Ash swears the crew to secrecy, revealing that half of them are gifted and hiding. He tells her the court's hunters have been taking people for months, not weeks. Emotional beat: solidarity forged in fear; Ash's hidden tenderness.

chapters.title: The Road Under Watch
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The crew travels inland toward Hollowmere, passing villages with empty doorways and painted thorn-sigils on thresholds. They evade a hunter patrol led by the pale-eyed Inquisitor Serel. Emotional beat: mounting dread; the country itself is complicit.

chapters.title: Hollowmere's Empty Cradles
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In Hollowmere, they find the town hollowed—gifted families gone, an old woman hiding in a chapel who remembers Isolde. She tells Xanthe the court buys souls willingly sold, and that Isolde sold hers to save someone. Emotional beat: the sickening suspicion that Xanthe is the someone.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Pell, a former court clerk, decodes a stolen ledger: souls are recorded as debts, and Isolde Fairweather's entry names the buyer's purpose—the Thorn. The moon's thirteenth turn is three weeks away. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the clock starts in earnest.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain's Skin
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The crew enters the old miners' tunnels toward the underground court. Xanthe's magic resonates strangely with the stone, and fragments of memory she doesn't remember losing begin surfacing—her sister's face, a burning room, a signature on paper. Emotional beat: disorientation; her own past is a locked room.

chapters.title: The Court of Quiet Bells
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The underground court is beautiful and terrible: courtiers with borrowed voices, nobles wearing other people's mannerisms. Xanthe poses as a soul-broker's agent. She glimpses the Thorn—a black root grown through the throne itself. Emotional beat: horror dressed in silk; power's seductive rot.

chapters.title: A Voice Not Her Own
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A courtier speaks to Xanthe in Isolde's voice—the Thorn lets the court wear fragments of the souls it holds. Xanthe nearly breaks cover. Serel the Inquisitor appears, and Ash covers for her at a cost. Emotional beat: heartbreak weaponized; the enemy knows her weakness.

chapters.title: The Bargain in the Root
chapters.summary: Serel's POV. Serel, once gifted herself, explains the court's covenant: the Thorn grants the throne dominion over weather, harvest, and memory, fed by surrendered souls. She offers Xanthe a place—power, safety, and a memory of Isolde restored. Emotional beat: temptation made reasonable; corruption as a gentle voice.

chapters.title: What Xanthe Forgot
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Serel returns the first of Xanthe's sold memories as a taste: the truth that twenty years ago, Xanthe's uncontrolled storm killed their parents, and Isolde sold her own soul to buy Xanthe's exile instead of her execution. Emotional beat: devastation; guilt as the true inheritance.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Nears
chapters.summary: Pell and Corvin's POV. Outside, the crew plans the heist of the soul-vault while hunters close in on their safehouse. Corvin reveals he lost a son to the court; Pell burns her old clerk's seal. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve; the crew becomes a family.

chapters.title: The Vault of Held Breaths
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Ash's POV. The infiltration begins: through the flooded galleries to the vault where souls hang like lanterns. Xanthe finds Isolde's soul-light and reaches for it—and the vault seals. Ash's signal flare has betrayed them. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out; trust shattered.

chapters.title: Ash's Price
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Ash sold the crew's plan to the court to buy back his own stolen soul—the Thorn holds his daughter's. He begs Xanthe to understand; she cannot. Serel takes them to the throne room as the moon begins its final turn. Emotional beat: betrayal without villainy; everyone is someone's price.

chapters.title: Throne of Root and Bone
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Before the Thorn-crowned throne, the court offers Xanthe everything: Isolde's soul, her memories, her exile undone—if she surrenders her storm and serves. The Thorn whispers in her mother's voice. Emotional beat: the climactic temptation; power offering to heal the wound it caused.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe refuses—not with a speech, but by calling the storm she has suppressed for twenty years into the mountain's heart. The crew, freed by Corvin's sacrifice, fights through the galleries. Serel, seeing the Thorn's hunger unmasked, turns her key in the vault's lock. Emotional beat: catharsis; the storm as answer.

chapters.title: When the Mountain Sings
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The climax: Xanthe's storm meets the Thorn's root through the mountain's bones. Ash holds the collapsing vault open with his body; his daughter's soul-light touches his hand before rising. The Thorn shatters, and the court's stolen voices scream free. Emotional beat: terrible beauty; sacrifice as the only clean currency.

chapters.title: Souls in the Moonlight
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the ruin of the court, Isolde's soul passes through Xanthe—one breath of her sister's voice, forgiveness spoken—before rising with the others into the thirteenth moon's full light. The storm takes Xanthe's magic as its price. Emotional beat: release and loss braided together; the inheritance finally set down.

chapters.title: A Charm for Greyharbor
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A year later, magic is no longer hunted, and Greyharbor's market is loud with open charm-sellers. Xanthe, magicless, teaches knot-work to Wren, who has the gift. She ties one last charm and hangs it for Isolde. Emotional beat: quiet peace; power ends, but inheritance—chosen this time—continues.
